# Round 2 — the review-guard conflict, settled by measurement

**Answer: (d).** The review-heading regex is the wrong instrument at the wrong granularity, in arm 4b *and* in the fallback. (a), (b), (c) are three points on one axis and I measured all three; none is right. Two of the brief's load-bearing premises are also wrong, and I show why.

---

## 1. The `**` blind spot does not exist

The brief measured the regex on the **raw** reply. The parser never sees raw text: `runner_core.py:440` runs `response = re.sub(r'\*{2,}', '', response)` *before* both arm 4b's guard and the fallback's.

```
raw head        : '**Round 8 Review — `bench/macrophage_cell.py`'
guard on RAW    : False    <- what the brief measured
head after line-440 strip: 'Round 8 Review — `bench/macrophage_cell.py`'
guard on PARSED : True     <- what the code actually sees
```

So the premise "the guard does not fire on exp43, and the fallback shares the blind spot" is false. **There is no `**` blind spot to repair in either guard.**

## 2. But the guard still isn't what suppressed C0040

`_is_registry_prose = cid_prose(...) or review_regex(...)`. Python short-circuits, and on that reply `cid_prose` is `True`. Both disjuncts fire; the C-id one fires first. And the brief is right that arm 4b is unreachable: **0 markdown F-headings** on that reply. So the guard's stated justification is doubly hollow — it never fired alone on the case it was added for, and it could not have applied in 4b.

Load-bearing test, whole archive (5,698 replies): replies where the fallback's review-regex is the **sole** suppressor = **1**. That one is CC2-SIM r0 — a genuine blind first-pass review. With arm 4b repaired, it is **0 of 3,193**. In the fallback, the review-regex is dead code whose only unique historical effect was to delete a real review.

## 3. What the guard actually costs — measured across the whole archive

Guard A fires on 51 replies; fires **and** the reply carries md F-headings (i.e. actually blocks arm 4b) on **4 distinct replies**, all in `sim45_memory_20260901T003907Z`. Zero in ~5 months of prior experiments. I read two in full: both are novel, tool-executed, registry-hygienic. r1 ChatGPT-SIM ships an executed falsifier printing `FALSIFIED`; its stored metadata records `findings_count: 0`.

| | rehearsal r0–r3 | archive (5,698 replies) |
|---|---|---|
| HEAD (no 4b) | 10 | 14,369 |
| (a) guard as written | 29 | 14,527 |
| (b) tightened | 34 | 14,536 |
| (c) no review guard | 37 | 14,542 |
| **(d) per-heading content test** | **37** | **14,532** |

**A ⊂ B ⊂ C strictly and monotonically, per reply.** They are not mutually exclusive and not complementary — one axis, three thresholds. (d) is off that axis: `d=1` where `a=8`.

**The brief's claim for (b) is round-0-only.** "Admits both rehearsal replies, excludes nothing that currently parses" holds for round 0. Over rounds 0–3, (b) still deletes r1 ChatGPT-SIM (2 findings) and r2 Fable-SIM (1) — `## Round 1 Review —` and `## Round 2 Review —` fire the tightened form too.

**(c)'s stated rationale is unsound.** Importing the C-id prose guard into 4b would kill **39 of 104** (38%) archive replies carrying md F-headings. It is anti-correlated with what we want: r2 Fable-SIM cites C0002–C0004 *precisely to say it is not re-filing them*. Good registry hygiene trips the test. (c) also has a real residual — a synthetic summary with F-headings and empty bodies mints 2 findings under (c).

## 4. Arm 4b's real defect, which no variant of the guard touches

`#{1,6}` matches a **Python comment**. Reproduced in ten lines:

```
arm 4b as shipped (a): [('M_F001', 0.5), ('M_F002', 0.5)]
FALSIFIED: a Python '#' comment line is parsed as a markdown F-heading and minted as a finding.
```

Live in the archive: `# F004: Check the pruning logic` inside pasted tool transcripts mints **12 spurious sev-0.5 findings with code-paste descriptions** across two `falsifier_matrix_2026-06-06` replies — **real models, June 2026, not simulated.** (a), (b) and (c) all ship these. This is a bigger, older, real-data defect than the one the guard was written for.

## 5. (d) — the repair, applied

Delete the reply-level review guard; test each heading's **body** for any schema field. A heading that restates a settled finding in a summary carries none; a filed finding always does.

Adversarial set (6 cases), findings minted:

| case | HEAD | a | b | c | **d** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C0040 shape (C-id headings) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | **0** |
| summary restating own F-ids | 0 | 0 | 0 | **2** | **0** |
| round summary, verdict bodies | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | **0** |
| prompt-echo schema template | 0 | 0 | **1** | **1** | 1 |
| fenced schema echo | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | **0** |
| genuine blind first-pass | 0 | **0** | 1 | 1 | **1** |

(d) is the only variant that gets the genuine case *and* the summary case right. It does not catch the prompt-echo template (nor does b or c; only a does, by accident) — that shape occurs **zero times in 5,698 replies**, and such a finding lands unverified at the falsification gate. I am not adding a guard for a shape with no observed instance.

Suite: **9 failed / 4,685 passed** — byte-identical at true HEAD (`git stash`), with the round-1 repairs, and with (d). No new failures.

## 6. Where the repair belongs

**Both places, differently.** In arm 4b: replace with the per-heading content test (applied). In the fallback: **delete the review-regex disjunct outright** — sole-suppressor count 0 of 3,193, and its only unique effect ever recorded was suppressing a genuine review. The C-id disjunct already covers C0040 and is correctly scoped there, where the output is one unstructured blob and the reply-level question is the right question. It is not the right question in 4b, where the unit is a heading.

## 7. Disagreements to record

- **The `**` blind spot is not real.** Measured on raw text; the code strips `**` first. This premise should not survive into round 3.
- **"(b) excludes nothing that currently parses" is false** beyond round 0: 2 replies, 3 findings.
- **"suite 4,680 passed / 0 failed" is not reproducible.** I measure 9 pre-existing failures at true HEAD (ledger/documentation-drift and quarantined model-written tests). Not caused by the repairs — but the round-1 report should not have claimed 0.
- **The entire measured cost of the guard is in simulated replies.** No real-model reply in the archive is affected by a/b/c/d's *guard* difference. The case for the *content test* rests on real replies. Say so when this is written up: the guard argument is sim-only; the comment-line defect is not.
- **A separate gap, unfixed:** `extract_falsifiers` returns `{}` for r1 ChatGPT-SIM's prose-labelled `FALSIFIER:` + fenced block. That reply's falsifier was never machine-attached under *any* variant. Worth a round 3.

The through-line: three reviewers argued over where to set a threshold on a reply-level heuristic, and the heuristic had never once done the job it was hired for while a comment-line bug beside it was minting a dozen fake findings from real models. **The guard is the wrong instrument. Drop it, and test the content.**
